taxonomy_note: Workflow routing only. Choose final root-cause taxonomy from supported evidence.

controls.boundary: Neo4j procedure/function execution and graph privilege delegation
controls.source_trace: Trace caller-controlled parameters through a permitted procedure into graph, file, network or process capabilities beyond the caller role.
controls.implementation_branch: Resolve database/graph privileges alongside EXECUTE PROCEDURE/FUNCTION, boosted execution and procedure allowlist/unrestricted settings. A procedure name alone does not establish filesystem/network capability. Inspect its implementation and the effective caller role; compare an intentionally allowed read-only procedure with the restricted operation in an isolated graph fixture.
controls.operational_method: Retain the procedure signature/mode, installed implementation and effective grants. Ordinary EXECUTE permits invocation under applicable caller privileges; EXECUTE BOOSTED governs elevation and does not itself permit invocation. Elevated execution needs both grants for that procedure, subject to the deployed deny/mode rules. Separately, unrestricted registration is a configuration/implementation trust decision, not the user invocation grant. Compare invocation denied, ordinary execution and authorized boosted execution on an owned graph/trace; a procedure name or loading flag alone proves no file/network capability.
controls.controlled_verification: Use an isolated synthetic graph and reviewed inert procedure; compare ordinary graph access with a forbidden delegated operation.
controls.false_positive_discriminator: Procedure installation or an allowlist entry is not an exploit without caller reachability and a protected consumer.
controls.remediation_acceptance: Constrain procedure implementation and execution privileges, verifying legitimate graph functionality and rejected delegation.
